newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dassault gave documents to Belgium in bribes probe.
newsitem.headline: Dassault gave documents to Belgium in bribes probe.

text.p: French industrialist Serge Dassault has handed over documents relating to a bribery investigation to the Belgian judiciary, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Sunday.
On Friday, the court in Liege, eastern Belgium, had lifted a year-old international arrest warrant against Dassault, but it was not clear what had prompted the move.
"I understand that Mr Dassault and his lawyers have passed documents to the Liege judiciary," Dehaene told Belgian television VTM.
He said he did not know wheter this was why the warrant had been lifted and denied that there had been political pressure on the judiciary to do so.

The court issued the warrant for Dassault in May 1996 as part of an inquiry into claims Dassault paid 600 million Belgian francs ($17 million) to political parties to secure a contract to fit air defence systems to Belgian F-16 jets in the late eighties.
Dassault, chairman of French aerospace firm Dassault Aviation, has denied all wrongdoing but has refused to come to Belgium to answer questions for fear of being arrested.
Belgian authorities in May 1994 imprisoned Didier Pineau Valencienne, chairman of French electrical engineering group Schneider, for two weeks in a corruption probe.
The Liege court issued the arrest warrant after Dassault's refusal to attend a hearing there.
Dassault told French radio on Saturday he was willing to testify in Belgium under certain conditions.
Several Belgian political parties are under investigation for allegedly accepting bribes from the French group.

In 1995, NATO secretary general Willy Claes, a Belgian economics minister in the late eighties, was forced to resign over bribes alleged to have been paid to his Socialist Party by Dassault and Italian helicopter maker Agusta Spa.
